head_commit.message:
fix: make mail claims atomic and keep paged lists current across routes

Reserve delivery quota in the same transaction as the send claim, bind list caches and pending requests to their own revisions, and retain explicit load-more intent through background refreshes.

Add 22 backend and 27 Node regressions, a real cross-route browser scenario, and observed stream-animation preconditions. Preserve prior checks and timeouts.

Agent and Composer are Chromium only; later chat checks are independently complete across their actual three-engine scope. Independent isolated-worktree fixes are not part of this run.

sprint_execution_failure.cause_limit: The raw Chromium IDs demonstrate a 54-row retained range with the correct moved index 49; its exact-50 wait fails. Their raw CI receipts do not by themselves prove the precise overlap responsible; a more-first, stable-refresh-second race is independently reproduced against the frozen controller.

sprint_failure.cause_limit: The raw Chromium IDs demonstrate a 54-row retained range with the correct moved index 49; its exact-50 wait fails. Firefox and WebKit fail waiting for 54 after the list more click. Their raw CI receipts do not by themselves prove the precise overlap responsible; a more-first, stable-refresh-second race is independently reproduced against the frozen controller.

failure_accounting.chromium_observation: The raw complete54 IDs exactly retain the original order with indexes49/50 exchanged and the moved ID at49; busy=false. The original HTTP first-page50 assertion passed, but the entire-DOM50 wait was incompatible with the legitimately retained54 range.
failure_accounting.firefox_webkit_observation: The first-page50 checks passed, then each more click timed out waiting for54. The receipts lack controller generations, so the exact CI overlap remains an inference. The inverse append-first/refresh-second race was separately reproduced on the actual frozen controller.
failure_accounting.clock_cases: All three engines passed the real warm and measured revision equality, sparse HTTP200, exact54 IDs, zero full-page reads/DOM mutations and retained focus/scroll.
